items.headline: Winter Camp: Sign Up Now
items.body: Elite FC Winter Camp runs Dec. 27–31, 9:30 a.m. to 2 p.m., and it's open to all levels: footwork, technical and tactical drills, and games. Dec. 27 starts with a swag giveaway. K2 Fitness runs strength and conditioning on Dec. 28 and 30. On Dec. 29, a professional instructor leads yoga and breath control for competition, and lunch is served. Crepes on Dec. 31 celebrate the end of camp and 2026. Call it a tune-up for the second half of the season, or a good excuse to escape visiting relatives for a few hours. If you're going, let the club know as soon as possible for a headcount; contact the club for price and sign-up.

items.headline: Photo from History: 2000–2004 — Back-to-back in Sydney and Athens
items.body: Tímea Nagy met Laura Flessel at two decisive stages of her Olympic career. In Sydney in 2000, she edged the reigning champion 15–14 in the semifinal before beating Switzerland’s Gianna Hablützel-Bürki 15–11 for gold. Four years later, Nagy and Flessel faced each other in the Athens final; Nagy won 15–10 to retain the individual epee title. The Hungarian announced her retirement after Athens, then changed her mind and won the 2006 individual world championship. Her eventual retirement came in 2010. The photograph is a later portrait, taken at the women’s team epee award ceremony at the 2013 World Championships in Budapest.
items.caption: Hungary’s Tímea Nagy won Olympic individual epee gold in Sydney in 2000 and defended her title in Athens in 2004. After reversing a retirement announcement, she became individual world champion in 2006. This portrait comes from a 2013 ceremony in Budapest.
items.credit: Photo: © Marie-Lan Nguyen / Wikimedia Commons, “Award ceremony EFS-EQ 2013 Fencing WCH t215801.jpg”, CC BY 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Award_ceremony_EFS-EQ_2013_Fencing_WCH_t215801.jpg. No changes.
items.alt_text: Tímea Nagy in a pale yellow dress and long dark necklace, shown in three-quarter profile against a black background.
items.vet_notes: Cross-issue history pile, unvetted. Follows No. 5's Flessel (she lost to Nagy in 2000 semi and 2004 final). Cautions: non-action 2013 portrait; 2006 = individual world title; if cropped/grayscaled, change credit closing clause per CC BY 3.0. Women's epee at Dakar YOG is Nov 10.
